obligations.description: Per-cycle acceptance, order preservation, fixed latency, and bubbles
obligations.setup: After reset deassertion, drive special/finite inputs back-to-back using s_spec/s_sweep, and interleave single-cycle and multicycle bubbles using s_gap and s_rand; driving follows the existing clocking block phase and does not wait for DUT output.
obligations.expected: valid_o equals the synchronous pipeline marker for valid_i accepted 44 edges earlier; every cycle in which an output is expected has one corresponding result, with no extra results during idle and drain periods.
obligations.sampling: After an input is accepted on rising edge n, the output is valid after the NBA update on edge n+44; the pre-edge monitor reads it on edge n+45.
obligations.checker: The monitor samples actual valid and independent native model valid on every non-reset edge; the scoreboard performs exact four-state comparisons and also reports an error when expected is valid but actual is invalid; data is compared only when expected is valid, and the count must reach at least 1000 valid comparisons.

obligations.description: Synchronous reset and clear flush in-flight valid markers
obligations.setup: s_clear applies clear after a continuous sequence of finite numbers is already in flight, allows a full 60 cycles for draining, and then drives new data; s_rst pulses rst during a continuous stream and then resumes legal inputs; the initial rst spans at least two rising edges.
obligations.expected: Cleared old tokens are no longer valid; new tokens after resumption have normal ordering and latency; invalid result_o/invalid_o are not required to be 0.
obligations.sampling: Assertion between edges imposes no asynchronous clearing obligation; valid_o is immediately 0 after an edge with reset/clear, and resumes with the fixed latency after acceptance restarts.
obligations.checker: The independent model clears only the 45-bit tokens while continuing to predict data shifting; the scoreboard compares valid cycle by cycle, then compares data and flag in legal valid cycles; the reset task of the original interface does not force any internal signals.

obligations.description: Zeros, subnormals, and quantization of very small magnitudes

obligations.expected: When the Q5.16 magnitude m=0, the result is strictly 0.5 and invalid equals the input; nonzero m enters the finite approximation arithmetic rules.
obligations.sampling: Each input is quantized independently and then output after the fixed latency; bubbles do not change the numerical value.
obligations.checker: The native model quantizes according to the input fields; when the model outputs 0.5, the scoreboard compares exactly, without using ordinary finite-value tolerance to mask this exact behavior.

obligations.description: Fixed-point approximation in the finite domain and sign branches
obligations.setup: s_sweep performs directed sweeps of 96 points in the negative domain 0..16, 24 points in 0..1, and 128 points at k/8, while s_spec supplies points such as positive 1 and positive pi; s_rand mixes the actual runtime seed into the LCG starting point and samples 32-bit finite inputs; the numerical stream resumes around bubbles, clear, and reset.
obligations.expected: The exact reference is the fixed-point interpolation and rounding of the source RTL: exp quantization range=RNE(m*94548/65536), with linear interpolation and RNE between nearest-integer Q1.23 anchors for 2^(-k/16); the denominator is FP32 RNE 1+e, the reciprocal interpolates nearest-integer Q1.23 anchors for 1/(1+k/16), and the negative branch then performs FP32 RNE multiplication. The same native model produces exact FP32 bit patterns using independent scalar integer operations, mathematically generated anchors audited for consistency, nearest-even exponent alignment, and 48-bit mantissa multiplication; valid outputs must be bitwise equal, without using a real-valued sigmoid or numerical tolerance.
obligations.sampling: The numerical value is aligned with the sign and invalid of that input by the fixed latency; back-to-back sign changes must not cause cross-talk.
obligations.checker: The same self-contained model.sv consumes only native inputs and history for each profile and generates independent expected values aligned to 45 slots; the monitor samples actual/expected in the stable valid window, and the scoreboard reports errors using four-state inequality !== for valid, invalid, and all 32 bits of result. Compare valid every cycle to catch missing or extra outputs; D reuses the same file and exact comparison.
